control_was_live: The unpinned arm fired in both blocks, 4 of 8 and 7 of 8, so the lever was live throughout. windows-desk's promotion experiment on this issue was void for exactly the opposite reason - their control came back null - and interleaving is what makes this one not void.
design: interleaved pairs, same session, alternating arm by run
means: Leaving a single core free removes the lever: 1 of 16 against 11 of 16, p = 5e-05. The load is identical in both arms - 16 busy threads - and only its affinity differs.
not_claimed: That wakeup latency is the mechanism. It is consistent with these two results and no latency was measured. Cache and memory-bandwidth pressure are not excluded either: pinning the load to 7 cores reduces neither much, which is an argument against them and not a test of them.
reconciles_with_nice: Together with the nice result these say the mechanism is core AVAILABILITY, not scheduler SHARE. nice 19 load still breaks it, so the reader is not losing share; one free core fixes it, so what the reader needs is somewhere to be woken immediately. Consistent with wakeup latency when every core is occupied.
